new_symbol_range_suggestions.K_S_protect: positive; on the order of the substrate concentration range where substrate-rich conditions begin to noticeably buffer direct product-mediated catalytic suppression

derivation_notes: The direct catalytic suppression term is refined so that accumulated product inhibits turnover less effectively when substrate is abundant, represented by a substrate-dependent increase in the effective inhibition scale K_I_cat*(1 + S/K_S_protect). This keeps the existing states and mass-balance structure intact while adding a mechanistically plausible S-P interaction in the scored product-formation law.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that direct product-mediated catalytic suppression depends only on P by allowing substrate abundance to partially protect catalysis. This creates an observable S-P interaction in dP_dt at fixed C and P, especially during the late transient and depletion phases.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Direct product-mediated suppression of catalytic turnover is determined solely by product concentration and is independent of the contemporaneous substrate environment.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Substrate-dependent mixed inhibition of catalysis in which substrate-rich occupancy partially protects the catalytic conformation from direct product-mediated turnover suppression.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when substrate protection vanishes, for example in the limit K_S_protect -> oo so that K_I_cat*(1 + S/K_S_protect) -> K_I_cat.

response_change.parent_relation: The catalytic term depends only on accumulated product through k_cat*C/(1 + (P/K_I_cat)**n_I_cat), so at fixed P and C the instantaneous product-formation contribution is independent of substrate level S.
response_change.child_relation: Retain product suppression but let direct turnover suppression depend jointly on product accumulation and substrate occupancy, so that at the same P and C the effective catalytic inhibition weakens when S is high and strengthens as S becomes depleted.
response_change.observable_effect: During late transient and depletion phases, two times with similar P but different S can show different dP_dt/C in the child, whereas the parent predicts the same value once C and P are fixed.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when product has accumulated to P comparable to K_I_cat and substrate is no longer overwhelmingly abundant, so product suppression is active while S still varies substantially along the trajectory.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early high-S portions and later lower-S portions already coexist on one batch trajectory; the same product level can be encountered with different substrate availability across trajectories or neighboring times, and holdout extends this contrast deeper into depletion where the substrate dependence of inhibition is stronger.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that substrate modulation of catalytic inhibition vanishes, e.g. a large substrate-protection scale or zero coupling strength so the turnover term depends only on P again.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: substrate-dependent direct product inhibition of catalytic turnover
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Substrate-dependent mixed inhibition of catalysis: accumulated product suppresses turnover less strongly when substrate is abundant, consistent with partial substrate protection of the catalytic conformation or reduced access of inhibitory product effects under substrate-rich conditions.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the catalytic response from a product-only suppression curve into a joint S-P law, so no single global retuning of k_cat, K_I_cat, or n_I_cat can reproduce different inhibition strengths at the same P and C across varying substrate environments.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: All elementary kinetic coefficients remain constant during the trajectory, specifically the product-suppressed catalytic efficiency depends only on P and not on the contemporaneous substrate environment.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Direct product-mediated catalytic suppression is buffered by substrate abundance through a substrate-dependent effective inhibition scale.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: k_cat*C/(1 + (P/K_I_cat)**n_I_cat) - k_on_P*(E_total - C - EP)*P/(1 + P/K_I_P) + k_off_P*EP
evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_cat*C/(1 + (P/(K_I_cat*(1 + S/K_S_protect)))**n_I_cat) - k_on_P*(E_total - C - EP)*P/(1 + P/K_I_P) + k_off_P*EP
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered in the limit K_S_protect -> oo, which removes substrate protection and restores the original product-only inhibition factor.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative turnover dP_dt/C is no longer a function of P alone after subtracting the EP exchange terms; when P is in the inhibitory range near K_I_cat, higher S shifts suppression onset to larger P, so late low-S portions of the batch show stronger catalytic depression than earlier high-S portions even at similar P and C.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this because the parent catalytic contribution is separable from S once C and P are given. Retuning k_cat rescales all catalytic fluxes, while retuning K_I_cat or n_I_cat only changes the global P-response shape; none can make inhibition weak at high S and strong at low S for otherwise comparable P and C across the admissible trajectory segment.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when product has accumulated to P comparable to K_I_cat and substrate is no longer overwhelmingly abundant, so product suppression is active while S still varies substantially along the trajectory.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early high-S portions and later lower-S portions already coexist on one batch trajectory; the same product level can be encountered with different substrate availability across trajectories or neighboring times, and holdout extends this contrast deeper into depletion where the substrate dependence of inhibition is stronger.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that substrate modulation of catalytic inhibition vanishes, e.g. a large substrate-protection scale or zero coupling strength so the turnover term depends only on P again.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes direct product-mediated suppression of catalytic turnover is determined solely by product concentration and ignores that substrate-rich occupancy can partially protect catalytic turnover from product-driven allosteric or mixed inhibition.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: All elementary kinetic coefficients remain constant during the trajectory, specifically the product-suppressed catalytic efficiency depends only on P and not on the contemporaneous substrate environment.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Substrate-dependent mixed inhibition of catalysis: accumulated product suppresses turnover less strongly when substrate is abundant, consistent with partial substrate protection of the catalytic conformation or reduced access of inhibitory product effects under substrate-rich conditions.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-environment assumption inside the catalytic inhibition term rather than add a wholly new species. The parent target mapping has a fixed product-only suppression shape: once C and P are known, the catalytic part of dP_dt is fixed, so any two observations with the same C and P must have the same turnover contribution regardless of S. In a closed batch reaction, however, substrate systematically changes from high to low while product rises, and product inhibition of catalysis can plausibly depend on the substrate environment because substrate occupancy or substrate-rich conformations can buffer product's inhibitory effect. The child therefore changes the response from a separable P-only suppression to a joint S-P interaction in the catalytic factor. Holding E_total and all other conditions fixed, compare periods where P is in the inhibitory range near K_I_cat but S is still high versus later when S is depleted: the child predicts a steeper late-phase decline in dP_dt/C than the parent because the same product burden inhibits more strongly at low S. This is a direct change to the scored target mapping, not merely to auxiliary trajectories, since dP_dt itself at given observed S,C,P changes. The mechanism is admissible without new degrees of freedom because S is already a tracked state. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast across such conditions: changing k_cat, K_I_cat, or n_I_cat only reshapes inhibition as a function of P globally, but cannot make inhibition weak at high S and strong at low S when P and C are otherwise comparable.

scenario_text: Follow a closed batch reaction in which substrate binds reversibly to an enzyme, forms a transient enzyme-substrate complex, and is then converted irreversibly into product. Substrate, bound complex, and product are jointly tracked from their initial values, while free enzyme is determined by a fixed total enzyme pool. The target is the instantaneous product accumulation rate throughout the transient and depletion phases.
